solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Race had become disorderly farce

indicators.note: something that has become disorderly has lost its order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A race descends into chaos and turns into a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' does double duty in the surface but is part of the letters being rearranged; 'become disorderly' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence that fools nobody, the same idea as a farce in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Desire firm check

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to vet is to examine closely

explanation.surface: A company wants a thorough audit carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective meaning resolute; it is the noun for a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to want something intensely, usually what belongs to someone else, which is a strong form of desire.

clue.text: Card game requiring absurd caution: cross!

indicators.note: something absurd makes no sense, so these letters are put into a sensible order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
to bridge a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: A card player warns that the game demands ridiculous care, and is cross about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an angry adjective; it is the verb for spanning.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is the older form of bridge, in which tricks bid for and won all count towards game.

clue.text: Something opponents may do to do the opposite

definitions.text: Something opponents may do to do the opposite

parts.words: Something opponents may do to do the opposite
parts.note: surface reading: rivals might act in a way that contradicts what they set out to do
setter's reading: the idiom where two sides consent to differ, so the word is the opposite of differ

explanation.surface: Rivals may end up doing the very reverse of what they intended.
explanation.walkthrough: Think of the phrase where people who disagree consent 'to differ': the answer is the verb that precedes it, and it means the opposite of differ.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about accepting disagreement, opponents consent to differ, so the word means to concur, the reverse of differing.

clue.text: It goes badly for bighead

indicators.note: done badly means done wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Things turn out poorly for a conceited person.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoist is self-centred and full of their own importance, which is what a bighead is.

clue.text: Near end of employment, a dark time

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of employment

explanation.surface: Someone nearing the end of their job feels it is a gloomy period.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the part of every day when it is dark, so it is literally a dark time.

clue.text: New climb just starting

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A mountaineer sets out on a fresh route up the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something newly come into being and beginning to develop, so it is just starting.

clue.text: Redirect gangs to be reformed as expression of friendship

indicators.note: to be reformed is to be formed again in a different shape

parts.note: the thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Youth workers steer gangs towards going straight as a friendly gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' suggests criminals turning over a new leaf; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending a card with greetings on it is a token of goodwill towards a friend or relative.

clue.text: Having finally left everything one can leave

definitions.text: Having finally left everything one can leave

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: the final letter of left
a person's estate is all the property passed on at death

explanation.surface: Someone who has at last bequeathed all their worldly goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a person who dies leaving a will has disposed of everything they could leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate describes someone who died having made a valid will, so they formally left their estate to chosen heirs.

clue.text: Brutality imprisoning a monarch for lack of personal experience

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut something inside, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: viciousness is savage cruelty
taken as written
R abbreviates rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A cruel regime locking up a king is condemned, oddly, for being out of touch.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R together go inside VICIOUSNESS, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicariousness is experiencing things second-hand through other people, which means having no direct experience of your own.

clue.text: After short time, added piece that can give more power to your elbow

definitions.text: that can give more power to your elbow

parts.note: a trice is an instant
PS is a postscript, a piece added to a letter

explanation.surface: After a brief pause, a bolted-on part gives extra power, like an encouraging slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More power to your elbow' is a British idiom wishing someone success; here it is read literally, since this muscle straightens the elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm extends the elbow joint, so it literally powers that joint.

clue.text: Insignificant actor in run — but no hit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a film ... with no lines
second meaning: in cricket, a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball, such as a wide or bye

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor appears in a show's run that never became a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a theatre run; it is a cricket run. Cricket credits runs from byes and wides to the team, not the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a background performer in a crowd scene and a cricket run conceded without any stroke from the bat.

clue.text: Makes keener ahead of time, I assure you

parts.note: hones means sharpens, making a blade keener
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a person sharpens things before the deadline, truly.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as an exclamation, the word is a plea to be believed, just like protesting sincerity with a reassuring phrase.

clue.text: E.g. top ten names provided to dangerous criminal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a chart of the most popular songs
second meaning: a roll of intended victims handed to an assassin

explanation.surface: A top-ten list of names is handed over to a violent gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a chart of popular hits and a list of people targeted for killing by a hitman.

clue.text: Problem about dreadful cant in sacred place

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are mangled
about means around, so one part goes round the other

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone objects to awful hypocritical talk being spoken in a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: Cant is hypocritical pious talk, which suits a church surface, but here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is the holy inner part of a temple or church, a sacred place, or by extension a private retreat.

clue.text: For example, join in with this position

indicators.note: the word sought is what you join to 'in' to make the example phrase, so 'in' is stripped off

parts.note: 'for instance' means for example, so instance stands for it

explanation.surface: An instruction: as an illustration, take up this posture together.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put IN before the answer and you get INSTANCE, as in 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is the way a person stands or the view they take, both of which are a position.

clue.text: Repeated part of song about ancient deity

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for circa, about
Horus is the falcon-headed god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A recurring verse in a hymn concerns an old god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the subject of'; it is c for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: The chorus is the refrain sung after each verse, the section of a song that recurs.

clue.text: Revolution engulfing one European city

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so one part ends up inside the other

parts.note: a turn is one revolution
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A political uprising sweeps through a single city in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major industrial city in northern Italy, the capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Humdrum reporter saying it's useful for cutting

parts.note: a hack is an uninspired journalist
a saw is an old proverb

explanation.surface: A dull journalist's remark is said to be handy for trimming copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saying' looks like a verb on the reporter; it is the noun for a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed handsaw in a frame, a tool for cutting metal and plastic.

clue.text: Dishes from large part of the world

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the vast Asian country

explanation.surface: Cuisine originating from a big region of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both porcelain crockery and the huge East Asian nation where such ware originated.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement's superficial mark, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the answer only matches it in pronunciation

parts.note: a weal is a raised mark on the skin's surface

explanation.surface: A rebel group's damage is only skin-deep, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary movement' suggests politics; it means turning round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns on its axle, so its motion is revolution in the literal rotating sense.

clue.text: Stop male, one in natural setting that's undefined

indicators.note: the pieces before it are placed in the setting that follows

parts.note: innate means natural, inborn; 'setting' marks it as the surround
to deter is to put someone off, stopping them
M is the standard abbreviation for male
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Halt a man, one in a wild landscape whose identity is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural setting' suggests countryside; it is INNATE, which holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indeterminate has not been fixed or settled, so it is vague and undefined.

clue.text: Amount of heat concealed by weathermen

indicators.note: something concealed by a word is tucked inside its letters

parts.note: sits inside the word, after its first two letters

explanation.surface: TV forecasters keep quiet about how warm it will actually be.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat energy, formerly used in Britain for billing gas supply.

clue.text: Combination of scandium with other metal — that's shocking

parts.note: Sc is the chemical symbol for scandium
and means together with
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A chemist mixes scandium with another metal and is appalled at the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' hints at electricity in a chemistry setting; it means outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a disgraceful event that causes public outrage, so it is something shocking.
